<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by converting A's massacre concession into a live decision rule: citizens own schools, but evidence can overrule a majority on the baseline, and that veto should hit before homework. A's "selection is the sermon" and camouflage/accountability critique stayed sharp and never fully died, yet B's split-reporting answer and child-in-the-room weighing made the comparative easier to vote. A's later floor-versus-ceiling line was strong crystallization, not a new case, and did not restore a standard of falsehood independent of the next board.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's massacre question forced A to admit a board that denies documented fact "abuses" citizen authority; B then used that admission, especially in rebuttal 2 and closing, to collapse A's thin brute-fact/framing line into the motion's actual capture problem.</best_rebuttal>
